docs.title: Welcome to Prompt Optimization Agent
docs.text: A production-grade prompt optimization and reliability engine that transforms raw ideas into structured, validated, and enterprise-ready AI instructions.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 5 Output Modes: General LLM, Custom GPT, Agent, JSON, OpenAPI Action Schema
  • Prompt Hardening: Anti-hallucination safeguards, clarification rules, edge case handling
  • Risk Detection: Identify failure points, ambiguity, and safety risks
  • Metadata Generation: Version tracking, complexity analysis, model targeting
  • Iterative Improvement: Automatic refinement based on review feedback

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • Ollama (for local LLM support)

docs.title: Installation Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone and Enter:

    git clone <repo_url>
cd prompt-optimization-agent

  2. Environment Setup (Recommended): Using uv for lightning-fast package management:

    uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Linux/Mac
# .venv\Scripts\activate  # Windows
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

  3. Configure Environment: Copy the example environment file and add your credentials:

cp .env.example .env

!!! warning "Environment File Mandatory"
    The `.env` file is mandatory. If you are using `litellm` (Cloud providers), you **must** provide the corresponding API keys in this file.

Note: For local Ollama usage, no API keys are required, but the .env file should still exist to load default settings.

docs.title: LLM Configuration
docs.text: Edit src/prompt_optimization_agent/config/settings.py to change the active provider:

docs.title: LiteLLM (Cloud)
docs.text:
PROVIDER = "litellm"
MODEL_NAME = "gemini/gemini-2.0-flash"

docs.title: OpenAI SDK (Official or Compatible)
docs.text:
PROVIDER = "openai"
MODEL_NAME = "gpt-4o" # or any compatible model
OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1" # you can change this to any other provider with updating their api key

You can also set OPENAI_BASE_URL in your .env file to use OpenAI-compatible services like OpenRouter, DeepSeek, or LiteLLM Proxy.

docs.title: Ollama (Local)
docs.text:
PROVIDER = "ollama"
MODEL_NAME = "llama3.1:8b"

Ensure the Ollama server is running locally before execution.

Additional Settings

You can also confirm all other env variables in .env file, such as MAX_TOKENS, TEMPERATURE, TIMEOUT_SECONDS, etc.

uv run prompt-optimization-cli

docs.title: Output Modes
docs.text:
The Prompt Optimization Agent supports 5 output modes:

Mode Description general_llm Standard prompts for ChatGPT, Claude, etc. custom_gpt GPT Builder configuration format agent AI agent system prompts json Structured JSON for APIs/automation action_schema OpenAPI 3.1.0 schemas for tool-calling

docs.title: Adding Custom Prompts
docs.text: Replace the content in the .md files in src/prompt_optimization_agent/agent/prompts with your instructions. Default templates are already optimized but can be customized as needed.

docs.title: Testing Guide
docs.text: This document outlines procedures for testing the Prompt Optimization Agent.

docs.title: 1. Automated Unit Tests
docs.text: The project includes comprehensive unit tests in tests/ directory. Tests use mocks for LLM providers.

docs.title: Using Pytest (Recommended)
docs.text:
# Install test dependencies
uv pip install pytest pytest-mock pytest-cov

# Run the full suite
uv run pytest tests/

docs.title: Using Unittest (Built-in)
docs.text:
python3 -m unittest discover tests

# Run with verbose output
python3 -m unittest -v discover tests

docs.title: CLI Testing
docs.text:
python -m prompt_optimization_agent.cli

Verification Points:

  • Mode selection works (1-5 options)
  • Pipeline initializes without errors
  • Iteration status is displayed
  • Risk analysis is shown
  • Hardened prompt is displayed
  • Output format toggle works (m/j)

docs.title: Web UI Testing
docs.text:
streamlit run src/prompt_optimization_agent/ui.py

Verification Points:

  • Mode selector in sidebar works
  • Output format toggle works
  • Progress bars/status update correctly
  • Risk analysis section displays
  • Metadata section displays

docs.title: 3. Code Style & Linting
docs.text:
# Check for style issues
uv run ruff check .

# Automatically fix minor issues
uv run ruff check . --fix

docs.title: 4. Test Structure
docs.text:
• tests/test_agents.py: Tests for PromptOptimizer, PromptHardener, RiskDetector, PromptReviewer, TestCaseGenerator, and Orchestrator
  • tests/test_providers.py: Tests for OpenAI and Ollama providers
  • tests/test_exporter.py: Tests for markdown generation
  • tests/test_core_utils.py: Tests for InputConfig, ComplexityAnalyzer, MetadataGenerator
  • tests/test_memory_loading_verification.py: Tests for MemoryManager

docs.title: Mode Selection
docs.text:
Test all 5 output modes:

  • general_llm - Standard prompts
  • custom_gpt - GPT Builder config
  • agent - AI agent prompts
  • json - JSON output
  • action_schema - OpenAPI schemas

docs.title: Risk Detection
docs.text:
Verify risk analysis returns:

  • overall_risk_score (0-10)
  • risk_level (low/medium/high)
  • risks list with categories
  • recommendations list

docs.title: Prompt Hardening
docs.text:
Verify hardening adds:

  • Anti-hallucination safeguards
  • Clarification rules
  • Edge case handlers

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: The Prompt Optimization Agent can be used through two interfaces:

docs.title: 1. CLI Usage
docs.text:
Run the interactive command-line interface:

uv run prompt-optimization-cli
  • Mode Selection: Choose from 5 output modes (General LLM, Custom GPT, Agent, JSON, Action Schema)
  • Output Format: Choose between Markdown or JSON output
  • Workflow: The CLI shows optimization progress, review results, risk analysis, and test cases
  • Export: Results are automatically saved to the output/ directory

docs.title: 2. Web UI (Streamlit)
docs.text:
Launch the graphical interface:

uv run streamlit run src/prompt_optimization_agent/ui.py
  • Mode Selector: Choose output mode from sidebar dropdown
  • Output Format: Toggle between Markdown and JSON
  • Live Status: Uses the st.status component to show real-time pipeline progress
  • Visual Review: See ratings and approvals with clear color-coded indicators
  • Risk Analysis: View detected risks and severity levels
  • Metadata: See version, mode, and complexity information

docs.title: 3. Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
The optimization pipeline runs through these stages:

  1. Optimize: Generate prompt based on user input and selected mode
  2. Review: Evaluate prompt quality and provide feedback
  3. Risk Detection: Analyze for potential failure points and risks
  4. Hardening: Add safety rules and edge case handling
  5. Test Cases: Generate validation test cases
  6. Metadata: Attach version and complexity information

docs.title: 4. Review Process
docs.text:
• If an agent rates the prompt below 4/5, the system will attempt iterative improvement automatically (up to 3 times)
  • Feedback from the review agent is used to refine the next generation

docs.title: 5. Output Management
docs.text:
• All final results are stored in output/ as Markdown files
  • Each file includes: final prompt, review audit, risk analysis, test cases, and metadata
  • JSON output is also available via CLI or UI

docs.title: 6. Mode Selection
docs.text: Mode Use Case general_llm Standard prompts for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini custom_gpt GPT Builder configuration with instructions agent AI agent system prompts with tool definitions json Structured JSON for API/automation workflows action_schema OpenAPI 3.1.0 schemas for Custom GPT Actions

docs.title: 7. Memory Integration
docs.text:
• The system uses memory for prompt engineering notes
  • Notes are stored in src/prompt_optimization_agent/agent/memory directory
  • Prompt templates are in src/prompt_optimization_agent/agent/prompts directory

docs.title: 🔹 What This Product Is (Simple Explanation)
docs.text:
This is a smart system that turns messy ideas into production-ready AI prompts.

Instead of just generating prompts, it:

  • Structures them properly
  • Reviews and improves them
  • Tests them
  • Scores their quality
  • Hardens them for real-world usage

It ensures prompts are:

  • Clear
  • Safe
  • Reliable
  • Reusable
  • Ready for any AI agent use

docs.title: 🎯 Problem It Solves
docs.text:
Most AI users:

  • Write vague prompts
  • Get inconsistent results
  • Face hallucinations
  • Don’t define output format
  • Don’t test edge cases
  • Can’t reuse prompts across teams

This tool solves that by turning prompts into structured, validated AI instructions.

docs.title: 🏗️ What It Actually Does
docs.text:
When a user provides an idea, the system:

  1. Converts it into a structured prompt blueprint
  2. Reviews and scores its quality
  3. Improves weak areas automatically
  4. Adds safety and anti-hallucination rules
  5. Generates test cases for validation
  6. Produces a final production-ready version

Optional modes allow generation for:

  • General LLM use
  • Custom GPT configuration
  • AI agent system prompts
  • JSON/API-based workflows
  • Automation-focused workflows

docs.title: BaseProvider
docs.text:
Abstract base class for AI providers.

Methods:

  • generate(prompt: str, system_prompt: Optional[str] = None) -> str: Generate a response from the AI provider.

Example:

from prompt_optimization_agent.interfaces.base_provider import BaseProvider

class MyProvider(BaseProvider):
    def generate(self, prompt: str, system_prompt: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
        # Implementation
        return "response"

docs.title: BaseAgent
docs.text:
Abstract base class for agents.

Methods:

  • run(input_data: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: Run the agent with input data.

docs.title: PromptOptimizationOrchestrator
docs.text:
Main entry point for the pipeline.

Methods:

  • __init__(provider: Optional[BaseProvider] = None, mode: PromptMode = PromptMode.GENERAL_LLM): Initialize with optional custom provider and output mode.
  • run_pipeline(user_input: str, max_iterations: int = 3, mode: Optional[PromptMode] = None, output_format: str = "markdown") -> Dict[str, Any]: Run full pipeline.

Returns: Complete result dict with generated_prompt, hardened_prompt, review, risk_analysis, test_cases, metadata.

Example:

from prompt_optimization_agent.agent.orchestrator import PromptOptimizationOrchestrator
from prompt_optimization_agent.core.config.input_config import PromptMode

orchestrator = PromptOptimizationOrchestrator(mode=PromptMode.AGENT)
result = orchestrator.run_pipeline("Generate a system prompt for an AI agent")

docs.title: PromptOptimizer
docs.text:
Agent for generating optimized prompts with mode support.

Methods:

  • __init__(provider: BaseProvider, use_memory: bool = True, mode: PromptMode = PromptMode.GENERAL_LLM)
  • set_mode(mode: PromptMode): Change output mode
  • run(user_input: str, previous_prompt: Optional[str] = None, feedback: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]

docs.title: PromptHardener
docs.text:
Agent for hardening prompts with safety rules and edge case handling.

Methods:

  • run(prompt: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: Returns hardened_prompt

docs.title: RiskDetector
docs.text:
Agent for detecting risks in prompts.

Methods:

  • run(prompt: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: Returns risk analysis with overall_risk_score, risk_level, risks, summary

docs.title: PromptReviewer
docs.text:
Agent for reviewing prompt quality.

Methods:

  • run(prompt: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: Returns approved, rating, feedback

docs.title: TestCaseGenerator
docs.text:
Agent for generating validation test cases.

Methods:

  • run(prompt: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: Returns test_cases list

docs.title: InputConfig
docs.text:
Configuration class for prompt optimization input.

from prompt_optimization_agent.core.config.input_config import InputConfig, PromptMode, ComplexityLevel

config = InputConfig(
    user_input="my prompt idea",
    mode=PromptMode.AGENT,
    complexity=ComplexityLevel.LONG,
    target_model="gpt-4"
)

docs.title: PromptMode Enum
docs.text:
Output modes for prompt optimization:

  • GENERAL_LLM - Standard prompts
  • CUSTOM_GPT - GPT Builder config
  • AGENT - AI agent prompts
  • JSON - JSON output
  • ACTION_SCHEMA - OpenAPI schemas

docs.title: ComplexityLevel Enum
docs.text:
Auto-detected complexity levels:

  • VERY_SHORT - Minimal command
  • SHORT - Light structure
  • MID - Balanced detail
  • LONG - Production-grade

Settings are loaded from src/prompt_optimization_agent/config/settings.py. Key variables:

  • PROVIDER: AI provider ("litellm", "ollama", "openai")
  • MODEL_NAME: Model identifier
  • TEMPERATURE: Generation temperature
  • MAX_TOKENS: Maximum tokens
  • USE_MEMORY: Enable/disable memory

docs.text: All methods include try/except blocks with logging. Failures return appropriate error dicts.

docs.title: Prompt Optimization Outputs
docs.text: This directory contains automatically generated results from the Prompt Optimization Agent.

docs.title: Automatic Generation
docs.text: Every time a prompt is optimized, a new markdown file is created.

docs.title: Filename Format
docs.text:
• Pattern: {short_title}_{timestamp}.md
  • Example: joke_writer_20260115_224002.md

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
Each generated file contains:

  1. Final Optimized Prompt: The copy-paste ready prompt
  2. Review Verdict: Approval status, rating (1-5), feedback
  3. Risk Analysis: Risk score, level, identified risks
  4. Test Cases: 5 scenarios to validate the prompt
  5. Metadata: Version, mode, complexity level, target model

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
When JSON output is selected, the result contains:

{
  "prompt": "optimized prompt text",
  "metadata": {
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "mode": "agent",
    "complexity_level": "mid",
    "target_model": "auto-detect"
  },
  "risk_analysis": {
    "overall_risk_score": 3,
    "risk_level": "low",
    "risks": []
  }
}
